short: How Does External Pressure Shape Li Dendrites in Li Metal Ba
title: How Does External Pressure Shape Li Dendrites in Li Metal Batteries?

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: How the stress state from external pressure shapes Li dendrites is unclear; coin and pouch cells differ in stress accumulation. Applying external pressure should shape plated Li smoother and denser and improve Li anode performance.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/gap), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/method), n4 (DES/variable_sweep), n5 (PRC/stimulus). Premises: Cycled Li|Li cells thicken by ~1.2 um per mAh (He and co-workers), building stress in rigid coin cells; Plating induces eigen strain, and mechanical energy enters the Gibbs free energy that sets the reaction rate

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Dendrites become shorter, less branched and stockier as external pressure rises. External pressure yields denser, less porous plated Li (higher space utilization)

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Pressure turns dendrite stress from tensile to compressive, maximal at the tip, inhibiting tip growth and promoting lateral growth. The mechanical driving force enters the interfacial driving force and slows the plating reaction: none below ~4 MPa, then linear, then saturating.
states.detail: Absorbed: n6 (MEC/pathway), n9 (MEC/pathway), n10 (PRP/value), n11 (PRP/value), n21 (MEC/tradeoff). Premises: Plating induces eigen strain, and mechanical energy enters the Gibbs free energy that sets the reaction rate; von Mises yield criterion: yielding once von Mises stress exceeds the yield strength; HY-6100 PP separator yield strength is ~20 MPa

states.title: Performance state
states.head: External pressure raises and stabilises Coulombic efficiency of Li|Cu pouch cells. Pressure shaping works only above a critical pressure that rises from ~1.2 to ~10 MPa as electrolyte modulus goes 0.2 to 2.0 GPa
states.detail: Absorbed: n12 (PRF/service_capability), n14 (PRF/service_capability). Premises: Porous, high-surface Li deposits expose more fresh Li to electrolyte, consuming Li and lowering Coulombic efficiency

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: For electrolyte-wetted PP separators apply more than 1.0 MPa, with the optimum no more than 5.0 MPa. External pressure inhibits Li electroplating and shapes dendrites smooth and dense but enlarges mechanical instability; a pressure-modulus diagram guides pressure design
states.detail: Absorbed: n15 (DSC/design_guidance), n17 (DSC/conclusion). Premises: PP separator elastic modulus is ~0.5 GPa, lowered by electrolyte immersion and porosity

nodes.title: ATOM, F2, F3
nodes.head: Without pressure p_m inside the dendrite is negative (to about -5 MPa) and near zero in the electrolyte. As pressure rises 2 to 14 MPa, p_m in the dendrite turns positive and peaks at the tip (red, ~15-20 MPa at 14 MPa).
nodes.solves: Pressure turns dendrite stress from tensile to compressive, maximal at the tip, inhibiting tip growth and promoting lateral growth
nodes.note: pressure levels read from column headers on F3a; at 2 MPa the dendrite interior is near zero/slightly negative (white-light blue) colour at the 14 MPa root reads ~12-15 MPa on the 0-20 scale; no region reaches the text's 19.5 MPa red

nodes.title: evidence, F4
nodes.head: Current density vs capacity curves sit lower for higher pressure; 12 and 14 MPa curves are lowest and end near 0.42-0.48 mAh cm-2. At 100 s, capacity falls from ~0.52 (2-4 MPa) to ~0.43 (12 MPa) and ~0.41 (14 MPa); current falls from ~21.2 to ~17.1-17.5 mA cm-2
nodes.solves: Electroplating rate falls with external pressure: at 100 s capacity 0.51 to ~0.41 mAh cm-2 and current ~20.5 to ~17.5 mA cm-2
nodes.note: text 0.51 to 0.41 mAh cm-2 and 20.49 to 17.44 mA cm-2; current minimum is at 12 MPa (~17.1), not 14; 14 MPa bar drawn in blue, off the colour gradient
